header.business: Example Dispatch Software, field service management software for HVAC, plumbing and electrical contractors, sold by a sales team on annual contracts (invented example)
header.source: CRM export (uploaded), call notes and interviews (pasted), platform leads (InsightfulPipe MCP)

overall.definition: Win rate = won / (won + lost). No decision is shown beside it and in the second rate.

headline_findings.finding: Our weakest pocket is Competitor B for buyers with 1-10 technicians: 27.1% win rate on 48 decided deals, against 48.3% overall. Discounts did not save them: lost deals there had a median discount of 15.0%, won deals 5.0%.

The reason logged at close often differs from what the buyer said: the logged reason matches a buyer reason on 50.0% of the 84 lost deals with a tagged reason. Price is the catch-all: 20 of the 32 lost deals logged as Price have no buyer reason that is normally logged as Price; they point most often to "Invoices would have to be re-keyed: no two-way accounting sync".
Long deals rarely close: deals that ran 91+ days won 17.5% of 63 decided. Won deals closed in a median 53 days, lost deals in 85.

LinkedIn Ads brings leads we rarely win: 358 platform leads became 43 deals and 10 wins (2.8 wins per 100 leads, win rate 31.2% against 50.5% for the cohort). Organic search turned 138 leads into 24 wins (17.4 per 100), the best of the tracked channels.

win_rates.rule: A cut under 20 decided deals is directional. Above or below means 20+ decided deals and a gap of 10 points or more from the overall win rate.

logged_vs_buyer_reason.rule: Shown side by side and neither is edited. The logged reason is the value the rep picked at close; the buyer reason comes from the deal-by-reason table built from notes and interviews. A deal agrees when its logged value is the value one of its buyer reasons is normally logged as.

loss_reasons.theme: Invoices would have to be re-keyed: no two-way accounting sync

evidence.text: operations manager, plumbing contractor, 50 technicians: "My bookkeeper said no the minute she heard she'd re-key every invoice."
operations manager, HVAC contractor, 29 technicians: "The other one talks to our accounting software. Yours doesn't. Simple as that."
owner, multi-trade contractor, 9 technicians: "We'd still be typing every invoice into the books twice. That was the end of it."

loss_reasons.fix: Build the two-way accounting sync, and until it ships say so in discovery and offer the CSV invoice export so it is not found in week three.

loss_reasons.theme: Go-live too slow before the busy season

evidence.text: service director, plumbing contractor, 110 technicians: "We needed to go live before the busy season and your date was after it."
service director, plumbing contractor, 108 technicians: "We needed to go live before the busy season and your date was after it."
Go-live estimate of six weeks was too long before the busy season.

loss_reasons.fix: Put a dated go-live plan in every proposal and offer a phased start (scheduling first, invoicing later) when the busy season is under eight weeks away.

loss_reasons.theme: Payback never shown; demo stayed on office screens

evidence.text: owner, electrical contractor, 10 technicians: "Nobody showed me what it saves per tech. I couldn't sell it to my partner."
owner, plumbing contractor, 3 technicians: "Nobody showed me what it saves per tech. I couldn't sell it to my partner."
owner, multi-trade contractor, 9 technicians: "It looked good, but I couldn't tell you what it saves per tech per week."

loss_reasons.fix: Lead the demo and the proposal with technician time saved per week and a payback month built from the buyer's own job count.

loss_reasons.theme: Per-user price above Competitor B for small crews

evidence.text: owner, HVAC contractor, 8 technicians: "Per user, you were the most expensive one we looked at for a crew our size."
owner, electrical contractor, 6 technicians: "Per user, you were the most expensive one we looked at for a crew our size."
Lost on per-user price; Competitor B's small-team plan undercut us.

loss_reasons.fix: Test a small-crew plan for 1 to 10 technicians instead of discounting; deeper discounts did not save these deals.

loss_reasons.theme: No offline mode for technicians without signal

evidence.text: Field lead asked twice about offline mode for jobs with no signal.
Technicians work in basements with no signal; our app has no offline mode.
Dropped after the pilot week: no offline mode when techs lose signal.

loss_reasons.fix: Add offline job notes and photos to the technician app; until then, test signal on site during the pilot.

evidence.text: owner, plumbing contractor, 7 technicians: "Having a named onboarding lead and a 30-day launch plan made it an easy yes."

operations manager, HVAC contractor, 49 technicians: "Route planning on our own job list showed the drive time we'd save. That sold it."

who.group: won against Competitor A or Competitor C

interview_guide.eligible_rule: Closed 2026-07-03 to 2026-09-30, not interviewed yet. Interview 2 to 6 weeks after close; the interviewer is not the deal's rep.
interview_guide.opening: Thanks for the time. We're not trying to reopen the deal; we want to learn how you made the decision so we get better. It takes about 25 minutes, and nothing you say goes back to the rep by name. Is it all right if I take notes?

items: What was happening in the business when you started looking?
What were you using before, and what had stopped working?
Who was involved in the decision, and who had the final say?
Which options did you look at, and how did each one get on the list?
Where did you first hear about us?
What did you expect from each option before the first call?
What did you need to see before you could say yes?
Which part of the demo or pilot stuck with you, good or bad?
What did your technicians or office team say after trying it?
How did you compare the prices you were quoted?
What did you expect it to save or earn, and did anyone show you that number?
Did a discount change anything for you? Why or why not?
What was the one thing that decided it?
If you could change one thing about how we sold to you, what would it be?
What would have to be true for you to look at us again?
